# The complete toolchain that compiles the backend dependency locks
# (src/backend/requirements.txt and requirements-dev.txt).
#
# Installed by `task deps:toolchain`, which is a prerequisite of both
# `task deps:compile` and `task deps:check` — and the "Lock staleness" job in
# .github/workflows/backend.yml (NFR-009 §2.3) runs `task deps:check`, so CI and
# a local recompile install the same file and pass the same flags by
# construction, not by two copies agreeing.
#
# Why the whole transitive closure and not just pip-tools
# -------------------------------------------------------
# pip-compile writes the invocation that produced a lock into the lock's header,
# and it reconstructs that line from CLICK's parameter metadata rather than from
# argv. A click minor bump therefore rewrites the header of a lock whose package
# versions and hashes are completely unchanged, and the staleness gate — which
# diffs the recompiled lock against the committed one — reports drift that no
# commit caused. That is what happened on 2026-08-27 (#1296): pip and pip-tools
# were pinned in the workflow, their transitive dependencies were not, click went
# 8.4.2 -> 8.5.0, and every backend pull request plus `develop` itself went red
# with the header comment as the only difference. Measured, not inferred: with
# pip-tools 7.6.1 held fixed, click 8.4.2 emits
#   `pip-compile --generate-hashes --no-strip-extras --output-file=… pyproject.toml`
# and click 8.5.0 emits the same line with `--no-index` inserted.
#
# What setuptools and wheel actually do here — measured, and not what an
# earlier version of this comment claimed
# -------------------------------------------------------
# This file used to assert that setuptools and wheel "reach the output the same
# way — they parse pyproject.toml [and] build metadata". For THIS project's
# pyproject.toml that is false. pip-tools 7.6.1 calls `build_project_metadata`
# with `attempt_static_parse=True`, and src/backend/pyproject.toml is plain PEP
# 621 with no `dynamic` dependencies, so `maybe_statically_parse_project_metadata`
# returns the dependency list and pip-compile never invokes a build backend for
# it. Its `[build-system].requires = ["setuptools>=75.0"]` is dead input to
# pip-compile; bounding setuptools there would fix nothing. Verified by
# recompiling both locks from an environment with setuptools and wheel entirely
# absent: exit 0, `git diff` empty.
#
# setuptools does reach the output — by a different route, one layer down. Two
# dependencies publish sdists only, aquacropeto 0.1.1 and http-ece 1.2.1 (via
# pywebpush), so pip builds THEIR metadata during resolution and reads their
# Requires-Dist out of it; that is what decides which transitive packages land
# in the lock. Under pip-compile's default build isolation, pip creates a
# throwaway venv per sdist and installs each sdist's own `[build-system].requires`
# fresh from PyPI, unpinned — the same floating input that produced #1296, just
# hidden behind a subprocess. Both `pip-compile` invocations therefore pass
# `--no-build-isolation` (see .taskfiles/backend.yaml, `deps:compile`), so the
# setuptools and wheel pinned here are the ones that render that metadata.
# Measured: content-identical output, the only change is `--no-build-isolation`
# appearing in each lock's header, which is why this pull request recompiled both.
#
# The residual exposure is named, not hidden. `--no-build-isolation` covers
# sdists whose build backend is setuptools, which is all of today's. A future
# dependency whose sdist declares another backend (hatchling, poetry-core,
# maturin, …) fails the compile with `BackendUnavailable: Cannot import
# '<backend>'` — loudly, attributably, and inside the gate rather than as a
# quietly different lock. The fix is to add that backend to this file.
#
# build, pyproject-hooks and packaging are pinned because pip-tools imports
# `build` at module load and `build` imports `packaging`; pip-tools also declares
# setuptools and wheel in its own metadata, so the `pip check` that follows the
# install fails without them. Their versions do not shape the output for this
# project — `build` is only reached on the non-static path this pyproject.toml
# never takes — but an unpinned member of the closure is exactly the gap #1296
# came through, so all six are pinned.
#
# `packaging` is deliberately held at the version BOTH compiled locks pin
# (26.2), not at the newest release. It is the one entry here that also appears
# in the backend's own locks, and `task deps:toolchain` installs into whatever
# environment is active: at 26.3 it left a developer's backend virtualenv
# running an unlocked packaging. Measured before choosing: 26.2 reproduces both
# locks byte-for-byte. Keep it equal to `packaging==` in
# src/backend/requirements.txt when the grouped Renovate pull request below moves
# either side.
#
# Deliberately WITHOUT --generate-hashes: Renovate's `pip_requirements` manager
# rewrites the version but cannot recompute a `--hash=` line, so a hashed file
# here would make every bot bump an uninstallable one. The pins are exact (`==`),
# and the install runs with `--no-deps` followed by `pip check`, so an unpinned
# transitive that a future pip-tools introduces fails loudly and attributably
# instead of drifting into the output.
#
# Renovate keeps these current through the built-in `pip_requirements` manager
# (this path is outside the `src/backend/**` disable rule in renovate.json5) and
# groups them into one "python lock toolchain" pull request. That pull request
# may legitimately move the locks — header or content — so recompile them in the
# same pull request when `Lock staleness` says so; the gate running there at all
# is why `.github/pip-tools-requirements.txt` is in backend.yml's `paths:`.
#
# click carries an extra `allowedVersions: '<8.5'` cap in renovate.json5, scoped
# to THIS file: 8.5.0 is the release that broke the header, pip-tools 7.6.1 is
# the newest release and is affected, so there is nothing to bump to yet. The cap
# does not touch the click in src/backend/requirements.txt, which celery needs.

pip==26.1.2
pip-tools==7.6.1

# Transitive dependencies of pip-tools, pinned for the reasons above.
build==1.6.1
click==8.4.2
packaging==26.3
pyproject-hooks==1.2.0
setuptools==84.0.0
wheel==0.48.0
